summary: Karpathy coined 'agentic engineering' (Feb 2026) and released Autoresearch, a 630-line ML automation system where an AI agent autonomously edits training code and runs experiments (reported ~100 experiments overnight). Signals general maturation of autonomous experimentation loops.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — inspirational for autonomous dispatch (HID-72) but no new concrete gap identified beyond existing issues

source: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2509.25140)
summary: Framework that distills generalizable reasoning strategies from an agent's self-judged successes and failures into a memory bank, retrieved at test time to improve future runs. Beats raw-trajectory and success-only memory on WebArena, Mind2Web, and SWE-Bench-Verified.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly maps to HID-188 (cross-run episodic memory for planner and executor). The 'extract from both successes and failures' insight is additive to HID-188 but the theme is already tracked.

summary: Non-gradient agent that edits its own code (tools, harness) based on LLM reflection; reports gains on SWE-Bench Verified from 17% to 53%. Notes that naïve self-correction can regress performance without external test feedback.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — supports the value of harness-level skill evolution (already partially shipped via distillationAgent.ts). The gap this would close is executor skill injection (mentioned in the Key Limitations list, not yet tracked as a standalone issue).

source: ODYSSE: Episode-wise Policy Optimization for Personalized Agentic Reasoning (arXiv:2607.25369)
summary: RL-based (ESPO, an episode-wise GRPO extension) approach for training agents on long-horizon personalized GUI tasks. Beats specialist GUI agents on the SmartSpot benchmark.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — RL-based training loops are a disqualifying red flag per the selection rules. AgentForge uses CLI subprocess agents, not trainable models. Out of scope.

summary: LangGraph 1.2 added per-call human-in-the-loop approvals, built-in MCP support, node timeouts, and DeltaChannel. CLI expanded with deploy list/delete/logs/revisions commands and distributed runtime support.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge is not built on LangGraph. The per-call approval and timeout patterns are interesting but AgentForge already has its own policy engine and state machine gates. No verified gap opened.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 GA (formerly AutoGen, April 2026)
summary: AutoGen moved to maintenance mode Oct 2025; Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 GA released April 2026 as successor. AutoGen repo now redirects to it.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses (Claude Code, Codex), not the AutoGen/MAF framework. Framework change does not open a gap.

summary: CrewAI continues active development; 1.15.18 confirmed Aug 2026, ~1.15.24 reported Oct 2026. Still focused on role-based crew orchestration.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses a different model (deterministic state machine + CLI subprocesses). No new capability introduced that maps to an untracked gap.

summary: ICML 2026 paper formalizes token/cost/time budget estimation for agents as progressive interval estimation mid-run. ACL 2026 SelfBudgeter adapts RL to set per-query reasoning token budgets based on difficulty.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — relevant to HID-163 (token cost telemetry). However the instructions explicitly defer budget/timeout optimizers until HID-163 provides measurement data. Theme already tracked.

source: GRASP: Generating, Revising, and Assessing for Strategic Planning (arXiv:2609.30147)
summary: Agentic AI strategic planning framework with generate-revise-assess loop. Details not fully retrieved from search results.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — plan revision loop maps to existing PlanRevision stage in AgentForge's state machine. Theme partly covered by HID-8 (plan rejection) and HID-93 (adversarial critique). No new untracked gap.

summary: Survey of multi-layer agent memory (working, episodic, semantic, procedural). Notes episodic memory is typically stored as conversation transcripts indexed by user/time + embeddings, with periodic compaction.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the compaction/consolidation pattern (turning episodes into generalizable facts) is additive to HID-188 but the core theme is already tracked there.
